prompt: The Grand Canyon Skywalk opened on March 28, 2007. It is owned and operated by the Hualapai Tribe at the Grand Canyon's western rim. The horseshoe shaped Skywalk extends 70 feet beyond the edge of the rim and is 4000 feet above the floor of the canyon. The Sears Tower, in Chicago, Illinois, is 1,450 feet in height. The height of a model of the Sears Tower is 9 feet 6 inches. A scale model of the Grand Canyon and the Skywalk is built to the same scale as the Sears Tower. What is the number of feet in the distance from the floor of the canyon to the Skywalk in the model? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Scale factor
solutions.body:
The model is $\frac{9.5}{1450}$ of real size. $4000 \times \frac{9.5}{1450} = \frac{38{,}000}{1450} \approx 26.21$ ft.

**Answer: 26.2 feet**

prompt: The Grand Canyon Skywalk is capable of supporting 71 million pounds. Assume the average weight per person on the Skywalk is 180 pounds and the maximum 120 people are on the Skywalk. What percent of the capable supporting weight is on the Skywalk? Express your answer to the nearest hundredth.

solutions.title: Find 1% first
solutions.body:
1% of 71,000,000 is 710,000 lb, so 0.01% is 7,100 lb. 21,600 lb is about $21{,}600 \div 7{,}100 \approx 3.04$ hundredths of a percent, i.e. $0.03\%$.

**Answer: 0.03%**

prompt: The driving distance from Flagstaff, Arizona to the entrance to Grand Canyon West is 216 miles. The estimated travel time is 3 hours and 50 minutes. If a car is driven these 216 miles in that time, what is the average speed of the car in miles per hour? Express your answer to the nearest whole number.

solutions.title: Convert time to hours
solutions.body:
50 min $= \frac56$ h, so the time is $3\frac56 = \frac{23}{6}$ h. Speed $= 216 \div \frac{23}{6} = \frac{1296}{23} \approx 56.3 \approx 56$ mph.

**Answer: 56 mph**

solutions.title: Miles per minute
solutions.body:
Time $= 230$ minutes. $216 \div 230 \approx 0.939$ miles per minute, times 60 $\approx 56.3$ mph.

**Answer: 56 mph**

prompt: The cost to build the Grand Canyon Skywalk was \$40 million. When the Skywalk first opened, the entrance fee to walk out on the Skywalk was \$25 per person. If \$15 of each admission fee went towards paying for the construction of the Skywalk, and if the admission fee was never raised, how many visitors would need to pay the entrance fee to recover the cost of building the Skywalk? Express your answer to the nearest thousand.

solutions.title: Divide
solutions.body:
$40{,}000{,}000 \div 15 \approx 2{,}666{,}667$ visitors, which is about 2,667,000 to the nearest thousand.

**Answer: 2,667,000**

solutions.title: Thousands of visitors
solutions.body:
Each 1000 visitors pay \$15,000 toward construction. $40{,}000{,}000 \div 15{,}000 \approx 2666.7$ thousand visitors $\approx 2{,}667{,}000$.

**Answer: 2,667,000**
